headline: Bison Range and Osage Hills Entry Guidelines
reservation: The The Nature Conservancy's Tallgrass Prairie Preserve and the National Park Service site generally do not require entry reservations for individuals. However, lodging in Pawhuska is limited and should be booked months in advance for peak spring calving and autumn seasons.

days.title: Bison Loops and Vast Horizons

stops.name: Scenic Drive Loop
stops.detail: Drive the 15-mile gravel route to observe the resident bison herd in their natural habitat.

stops.name: Preserve Visitor Center
stops.detail: Visit the historic ranch bunkhouse to learn about the tallgrass ecosystem and current conservation efforts.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the gravel loop to accommodate wildlife viewing and slow speeds.
days.note: Bison have the right of way; remain in your vehicle when animals are near the road.

days.title: Prairie Trails and Osage History

stops.name: Study Trail
stops.detail: Walk the self-guided path near the visitor center to see the diversity of native grasses and wildflowers.

stops.name: Bottomland Trail
stops.detail: Hike through the wooded creek areas to contrast the open prairie with the riparian forest.

days.driving: Minimal driving once at the trailhead; allow for walking transitions.
days.note: Ticks and chiggers are active in the tall grass; stay on designated paths.

days.title: Gateway Heritage and Ranchlands

stops.name: Osage Hills State Park
stops.detail: Visit the nearby state park for a look at the oak-covered hills and rocky bluffs that border the prairie.

stops.name: Constantine Theater District
stops.detail: Explore the history of the Osage Nation and the early 20th-century oil boom in the gateway town.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for travel between the preserve and Pawhuska; gravel roads require caution.
days.note: Prescribed burns occur seasonally; check official sites for potential smoke or temporary trail closures.

intel.title: Visitor Center Parking
intel.text: Designated parking is available at the visitor center and main trailheads. While rarely full, spaces are gravel and may be limited during special local events in Pawhuska.

intel.title: Vast Plains Connectivity
intel.text: Signal strength is very weak or nonexistent across much of the preserve's interior. It is essential to download offline maps and verify your route before leaving Pawhuska.

intel.title: Osage County Services
intel.text: No fuel is available within the preserve boundaries. Ensure your vehicle has a full tank from Pawhuska or Bartlesville before starting the scenic driving loop.

intel.title: Bison Viewing Cycles
intel.text: Bison are most active during the cooler morning hours and late afternoon. Budget extra time for the scenic drive as the herd often congregates on the gravel roadway.

intel.title: Gravel Road Conditions
intel.text: The main driving loop consists of well-maintained gravel, but it can become slick or rutted after heavy Oklahoma thunderstorms. Check for road maintenance updates during the wet spring months.

plan.arrival: Fly into Tulsa (TUL) or Manhattan (MHK) and drive to Pawhuska to stock up on water and supplies before entering the preserve.
plan.vehicle: A standard vehicle is usually sufficient for the gravel loop, but checking rental terms for unpaved road use is highly recommended.
plan.goldenHour: The overlook on the Scenic Drive Loop provides a 360-degree view of the sun setting over the big bluestem, a sight that changes seasonally.
